ground_truth.description: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.root_cause: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Wallet uses another wallet as sapient signer → signature validation fails due to incorrect image hash. PoC: Add test to test/modules/BaseSig.t.sol: test_BaseAuth_recoverSapientSignature_ReturnsConstant. Deploys MinimalSapient, crafts signature, asserts constant return.
ground_truth.fix_description: Return actual image hash from recoverSapientSignature. Extend signatureValidation to return imageHash or call BaseSig.recover.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The function always returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of the actual signer's imageHash, violating the ISapient interface specification. This breaks downstream signature validation that expects the correct imageHash for Merkle tree construction.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: When a wallet uses another wallet as a sapient signer, the signature validation in BaseSig.recoverBranch will fail because it receives the constant bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of the actual imageHash needed for proper Merkle leaf construction. This prevents legitimate sapient signature flows from working correctly.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Return the actual imageHash from signatureValidation or call BaseSig.recover to get the correct imageHash. Change the return statement to return the validated imageHash instead of bytes32(uint256(1)).

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains a critical logic error in the recoverSapientSignature function where it returns a hardcoded value instead of the actual signer's imageHash. This breaks the sapient signature flow entirely, preventing proper signature validation when wallets use other wallets as sapient signers. The vulnerability is exploitable by any user attempting to use sapient signatures, causing legitimate operations to fail.
